summary: Tested YouTube auto-publish flow end-to-end (no Google creds configured). 7/7 backend pytest cases passed. Frontend E2E: kicked full studio pipeline (espresso martini idea → TikTok script → voiceover → Sora hero render → final MP4 assembly, ~2 minutes), then verified the YouTubePublisher block appears, setup toggle reveals exactly 7 numbered steps, redirect URI pre-block shows the exact REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL + /api/youtube/callback, and clicking Connect surfaces a toast reading 'YouTube not configured — set YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID, YOUTUBE_CLIENT_SECRET, YOUTUBE_REDIRECT_URI in backend/.env' with the button remaining in disconnected state. All acceptance criteria for graceful degradation are met.
critical_code_review_comments: youtube_client.py stores refresh_token in Mongo in plaintext under _id='primary' — fine for single-user server-side use, but if this ever goes multi-tenant it needs encryption at rest.

youtube_routes.py _run_publish_job catches generic Exception and stores str(e) — good, but the created asyncio.create_task is fire-and-forget with no cancellation on server shutdown; consider tracking tasks in a set to avoid GC of pending uploads.
youtube_routes.py list_publish_jobs returns unbounded 50 docs with no auth guard — acceptable single-user, but worth noting.

In StudioPage.jsx line 968, the publish() polling loop runs 240 * 4s = 16 min inside a component; if the user navigates away the promise dangles. Not a bug for the current smoke test but a small robustness note.
YouTubeSetupHelp uses process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL directly — verified the URI matches backend/.env's YOUTUBE_REDIRECT_URI exactly, so no divergence risk today.
test_credentials: N/A — no Google creds by design
seed_data_creation: Test transiently inserts and removes a fake refresh_token doc in db.youtube_auth to exercise validation branches (privacy, traversal, mp3). Cleaned up in fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: YouTube publish flow is fully validated in the disconnected/misconfigured state. When real YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are added to backend/.env, next iteration should exercise: (1) /api/youtube/login now returns a real auth_url, (2) after manual OAuth, /api/youtube/status returns connected:true with channel_title, (3) actual upload of a small final_*.mp4 as private (not public) to avoid channel spam. The existing test file /app/backend/tests/test_youtube.py handles token-doc setup/teardown patterns and can be extended.
